newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BENGU CALLS FOR CALM ON HIGHER EDUCATION CUTS.
newsitem.headline: BENGU CALLS FOR CALM ON HIGHER EDUCATION CUTS.

text.p: Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu on Thursday tried to quell growing fears of massive cuts in government grants to universities and colleges, but warned that they would have to rethink spending.
He told the Committee of University Principals he had been lobbying hard to protect state grants and that a final decision could be made at the next cabinet meeting on February 5.
A finance department spokeswoman confirmed this was probably when the expenditure side of the whole national budget would be finalised.

There has been an outcry in academic circles in recent months over initial indications that the budgets of universities, especially the more privileged former white institutions, would be cut by up to eight percent.

This comes at a time when the formerly white universities are taking on more black students, many of whom have to be assisted financially. Steady budget cuts in recent years have also affected staff levels and research.
But Bengu warned that former white universities would have to accept some budget cuts to ensure that former cash-strapped black universities could improve their standards.
Heated negotiations have been underway in every government department over the past year to prevent swingeing cuts as part of the aim to reduce the budget deficit to 4.5 percent of GDP.
